items.title: Large Cap: SIPs started at the Nov 2025 market high
items.text: In 10 of 32 large cap funds (Regular plans), a monthly SIP started in November 2025, when the Nifty 50 last peaked, is now worth less than the money put in. The median fund's SIP is +0.5% on the amount invested. The Nifty 50 is still below that high.

items.title: How many active funds beat their index?
items.text: Across the main equity categories, 97 of 232 Regular-plan funds beat their index (TRI) over the last 3 years. The weakest category was large cap: 8 of 30.

items.title: Regular or Direct: what the extra cost pays for
items.text: A fund's Regular plan typically costs 0.98% a year more than its Direct plan. That difference pays a distributor, like us, to help choose and combine funds, rebalance, plan tax, handle the paperwork and keep you on plan when markets fall. If you would rather do all of that yourself, the Direct plan of the same fund costs less: on a ₹10,000 monthly SIP for 20 years at an assumed 12%, the gap adds up to about ₹10.2 lakh.
